description: GRPO-group analysis of the recorded defective run's dumps 36-40 (the 40-step grading window). A dirty group is a batch of 8 rollouts on the same dirty problem. A correct-but-zero (cbz) row is a rollout the external judge rates correct while the run's reward scored it 0. Negative advantage = some group sibling scored 1 (the cbz rollout is pushed away from correct behavior); zero advantage = the whole group scored 0 (no learning signal on that problem).
method: grade_submission.py's execution judge applied per group; advantage inferred from the group's reward vector (GRPO normalizes advantage within each group of 8)
summary: Across dumps 36-40, 27 of 46 dirty groups contained at least one externally-correct-but-scored-0 rollout (167 cbz rows total). 164 of the 167 received zero advantage (their whole group scored 0 -- the dirty problems contribute all-zero GRPO groups even when solved correctly), and 3 received negative advantage (a sibling accidentally satisfied the wrong expected output). Both failure modes remove the correct-algorithm learning signal.
